episode_title: Resilience is Expensive, Except in Retrospect - Michael Perron (FM)

real_qa.q: Why did FM Global and VDE separately verify Colin Sillerud's research on 75-degree panel stow angles at PVRW 2024?
real_qa.r: FM Global and VDE separately did the same research to verify Colin Sillerud of Groundwork Renewables' report on 75-degree stow angles. The verification confirmed that higher angle stow is better than lower-angle stow, but not as good as physics-based models alone suggest, confirming Collins' report was accurate. More work is needed on this topic.
real_qa.requete: FM Global VDE 75-degree stow angle verification

real_qa.q: What was the financial impact of major hail losses on solar insurers between 2019 and 2022?
real_qa.r: In 2019, insurers faced a $75 million hail event they were not expecting. Then in 2022, there were three big hail events in Texas that were all in the $30 to $50 million range. These significant losses made insurance companies nervous about the industry's resilience capabilities.

real_qa.q: What percentage of solar insurance losses does KWH Analytics data attribute to hail damage?
real_qa.r: KWH Analytics data suggests that hail losses are 73% of what insurers pay out, which means hail has an outsized area of emphasis with insurers because it is the biggest loss driver in the solar insurance market.
real_qa.requete: hail losses 73 percent solar insurance KWH Analytics

real_qa.q: How does FM Global's physics-based approach calculate panel resilience against hail in specific counties?
real_qa.r: FM Global uses internal hail maps developed by meteorologists for specific counties in Texas, then compares these to the design of the system being built, including which panel is used and stow angle. They calculate the kinetic energy that will hit the panel on a 1-in-50-year hail basis and determine how many joules of impact the panel needs to withstand, allowing them to specify the panel correctly for that angle and location.
real_qa.requete: FM Global kinetic energy hail damage panel specification

real_qa.q: What role do hail sensors play in solar project resilience monitoring and loss prevention?
real_qa.r: Hail sensors are not used to trigger stow—that would be too late since stowing takes 15 minutes—but rather to collect data on hail events. They are sophisticated plates connected to measurement devices that detect hail hits per second and average hail size. This data helps understand actual hail impact on sites, especially important for projects built on former farmland without good historical hail data, and provides learning value even when losses do occur.
real_qa.requete: hail sensors solar monitoring kinetic energy data

real_qa.q: Did insurers blacklist solar projects in Texas following major hail losses?
real_qa.r: One major renewable energy insurer stated they would not insure hail in Texas until the industry figured out resilience, which scared many stakeholders. However, that insurer had paid a $75 million sole-loss in 2019 and taken pieces of other big losses. That same company is now back in the business of insuring risk in Texas, though not fully confident everyone is doing it correctly, but closer than before.

His background spans underwriting, broking, and engineering collaboration, and he is now part of the management team leading FM Global's renewable energy market efforts. He has over 40 years of experience in the insurance space, with the last 10 years including a deep focus on renewable energy.
